title: Thy Bounteous Hand with Food Can Bless
description: Thy Bounteous Hand with Food Can Bless in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Reginald Heber wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 492, “Give Us Each Day Our Daily Bread”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy boun-teous hand with food can bless The bleak and bar-ren wild-er-ness, And Thou hast taught us, Lord, to pray For dail-y bread from day to day.

lines: Thy bounteous hand with food can bless
And Thou hast taught us, Lord, to pray
For daily bread from day to day.
And O, when through the wilds we roam
That part us from our heavenly home;
When, lost in danger, want, and woe,
Our faithless tears begin to flow;
Do Thou Thy gracious comfort give,
By which alone the soul can live;
And grant Thy children, Lord, we pray,
The bread of life from day to day!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Reginald Heber died in 1826.
credits: Words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
